title: What has just happened?
grammar: present perfect with just / already / yet (repaso)

scene.speaker: oliver
scene.bubble: Kili has just crashed into the window with today's mail! Don't worry — the window is fine. Kili too… more or less.

activities.title: Match the sentence with what it means.

she came in a second ago

items.sentence: Shhh! The baby has ___ fallen asleep.
I've ___ seen that film twice — let's watch another.
Look out of the window — it has ___ started to snow!

activities.title: Listen to the breaking news. Write a word in each gap.

data.voice_note: Voces: Oliver (testigo) y Kili (protagonista del choque).
data.script: Oliver: News flash! Kili has just crashed into the kitchen window. … Oliver: He's fine! He has already eaten three biscuits to feel better. … Oliver: The mail has arrived safely: two letters and one big yellow parcel. … Oliver: We haven't opened the parcel yet — it's for Ingrid. … Oliver: Wait… Ingrid has just come in! She's opening it… … Oliver: It's a new flag for the expedition! Blue, with a silver star. … Oliver: Kili has already forgotten the crash. He's flying loops around the flag!

data.text: Mime something that has just happened (you've just woken up, you've just won a race…). Your partner says the sentence: "You have just…!" Three mimes each.

activities.title: Look at A and B. What is different?
activities.instructions: Look at picture A and picture B. Find the 11 differences and tell your partner about them.

homework.prompt: Tonight, write 3 things that have just happened at home and 2 you haven't done yet: My mum has just… I haven't… yet.
